description: Synthetic offline cross-client credential conformance vectors with explicit shared parsing, selection, storage, and URL rules.

adapter_rules.absent: Omitted options are absent; map absent to JS undefined/Python None. Explicit Python None remains absence. Native JS null is an invalid supplied option and needs a separate native test; do not map a portable null wrong-type vector to Python None. Portable wrong types remain false, 0, arrays and objects.
adapter_rules.options: Map api_key/base_url/profile to each public constructor/startup spelling; MCP local paths only.
adapter_rules.file: base references base_document. In resolution_cases input.file may be a named fixture or a {base,patch} object. Apply all patches to own JSON members; never assign __proto__ onto an ordinary JS object. A schema_case has empty options/env unless supplied explicitly. Validate every resulting profile, including unselected entries.
adapter_rules.errors: rule is an observed semantic category, not an exact public class/message. Each adapter must derive its category from the actual refusal path; never catch an arbitrary exception and report the fixture's expected label. Assert zero HTTP and no secret-bearing diagnostics for every local refusal. Native result labels map explicitly to the same categories.
adapter_rules.zero_io: For credential_file_io=zero assert no home discovery, traversal, stat/lstat, open/read or parse of the credential store, including an accessor instrumented to throw if invoked. Module-loader IO does not count. input.home_discovery=throw_if_called names that accessor arrangement, not an already discovered home.
adapter_rules.required_io: required means file-backed resolution exercised, not a fixed syscall count.
adapter_rules.serialization: UTF-8 JSON without a BOM. bytes_utf8 and bytes_hex cases are authoritative raw payloads and must not be parsed/re-serialized before the tested reader sees them. Other size recipes compact-serialize then append ASCII spaces to the requested byte count.
adapter_rules.scope: Descriptive file metadata never grants server authorization.
adapter_rules.canonical_base: Apply canonical_base_cases to the new file/login canonicalizer only, never to legacy explicit/environment-key base resolution. bytes limits apply after the fixed trim. Stored base_url must exactly equal canonicalize(base_url). Positive bases must stay identical through transport construction/request path assembly.
adapter_rules.native: Each native_file_case has a 5000 ms end-to-end bound from starting the read attempt, including type refusal. Arrange the descriptor/directory race deterministically. F13/F14 may return the named original identity or a local error, never replacement identity. Unavailable wrong-owner evidence is explicitly reported, not passed.
adapter_rules.writer_deadline: Writer lock scenarios use a finite acquisition deadline configured and recorded by the adapter, distinct from the 5000 ms reader bound. The deadline never permits stealing or deleting another writer's lock.
adapter_rules.success: Credential success assertions compare the actual resolved source/key/base/profile. Schema success cases use the document default unless case options say otherwise. For foreign-surface error projections assert the established public representation and underlying status/reason, not an unavailable thrown class.

contract.base_binding: Only in the file branch, a supplied explicit base shadows environment base even if invalid/empty; validate it after the complete store and selected entry. Otherwise use a nonempty fixed-trimmed environment base. The winning override must canonicalize to the stored canonical base. No override means stored base. Legacy explicit/environment-key base behavior is unchanged per package.

trim.name: trimCredentialWhitespace
trim.operation: Remove only maximal leading/trailing runs of these code points. No Unicode normalization or interior replacement. No runtime-default trim/strip policy.
trim.emptiness: A trimmed empty explicit or stored key is invalid; an empty environment key/profile/base is absent. Accepted keys are returned trimmed; no API-key prefix requirement.

presence_and_order: Check supplied explicit key first: Python None/JS undefined are absent; other wrong types and trimmed empty values fail invalid_explicit_key with zero store IO. Do not inspect a lower-priority key, profile or file.

Otherwise a nonempty fixed-trimmed environment API key wins. Both key winners use existing package-specific explicit/environment/default base behavior and zero credential-store IO; unused profile selectors are not validated.

Without a key winner, select a supplied explicit profile (untrimmed), else nonempty fixed-trimmed environment profile, else defer to file default. Validate a known selector's complete grammar/reserved status before store IO; invalid_profile has zero store IO.

Then reject unsupported verified file protection with zero store IO. On a supported platform safely discover/check/open/read the store, enforcing exact modes/owner/type/link/size and native bounds; missing store is missing_credentials.

Strictly decode/parse the bytes, then validate the entire closed document and every entry, including stored default existence, before resolving the selected entry. A valid explicit selector does not excuse an invalid/missing default.

If a valid selected name is absent, fail missing_selected_profile. Validate/bind only the winning file-base override, or use stored base if none. Invalid/empty supplied explicit base is invalid_base_url even if environment base would match. Never fall back or make HTTP on a local error.

profiles.validation: Require a string with 1..64 ASCII characters: first A-Z/a-z/0-9; all remaining A-Z/a-z/0-9/dot/underscore/hyphen. Check the entire string, not a dollar-anchored match that can omit final LF. Reject exactly reserved_profile_names case-sensitively.
profiles.normalization: No trimming or case folding of explicit/stored profile names. Environment profile is fixed-trimmed before the same validation.
profiles.mapping: Use own properties. Reserved membership is the explicit list, not membership in a language prototype object.

canonical_base.input: Require string, apply the fixed trim, then require nonempty ASCII length at most 2048. Reject any remaining U+0000..0020, U+007F, backslash, percent, question-mark or hash anywhere. Require case-insensitive literal http:// or https://.
canonical_base.authority: Split authority before the first slash. Reject any at-sign in authority, an empty authority, malformed bracket syntax, empty explicit port or unbracketed IPv6. No repair, userinfo, query or fragment, even when empty.
canonical_base.dns: ASCII labels separated by dots; no trailing dot or empty label; each label length 1..63, ASCII alphanumeric/hyphen only, first/last alphanumeric; host length at most 253. Lowercase. No implicit IDNA or percent decoding; ASCII punycode labels are ordinary labels. A numeric-looking last label (all decimal digits, or 0x followed only by zero or more hexadecimal digits, ignoring case) is rejected unless the whole host is strict dotted-decimal IPv4. This excludes URL-parser numeric-host aliases.
canonical_base.ipv4: Exactly four decimal components 0..255, with no leading zero unless that component is exactly 0. Serialize those decimal components. Reject short, octal, hexadecimal and whole-integer forms.
canonical_base.ipv6: Bracketed valid IPv6 only, with no zone identifier or IPvFuture. Expand standard hexadecimal groups (and, when present, a strict dotted-decimal IPv4 tail into two groups) to eight 16-bit groups. Lowercase hexadecimal with no leading zeroes; compress the longest run of at least two zero groups, choosing the first on ties. Retain brackets.
canonical_base.port: If present require only decimal digits, numerical value 1..65535. Serialize without leading zeroes; omit 80 for http and 443 for https. Preserve other ports.
canonical_base.http: Canonical host must be strict IPv4 in 127.0.0.0/8, bracketed ::1, or exact lowercase localhost. Never resolve DNS or accept suffix matches. Login must explicitly select HTTP through a nonempty option/environment base; loading its saved canonical profile later counts as selecting that stored target. No default or fallback implies HTTP.
canonical_base.path: Empty or starts with slash. Each character is ASCII alphanumeric or one of -._~!$&'()*+,;=:@/. Reject any complete segment equal to dot or dot-dot. Percent and backslash were already rejected before parsing. Preserve case and interior repeated slashes; remove all terminal slash characters, including a sole root slash.
canonical_base.output: Lowercase scheme + :// + canonical host + optional canonical port + canonical path. Must be idempotent and stable through transport request assembly. Compare entire canonical strings, retaining origin, nondefault port and full path prefix.
canonical_base.stored: A file entry is valid only when raw stored base_url exactly equals canonicalize(base_url); do not repair noncanonical stored values.
canonical_base.scope: Only login targets and file-bound credential bases. Preserve current explicit/environment-key URL behavior independently in each package.

json_and_schema.decode: Strict UTF-8. A UTF-8 BOM is forbidden and produces invalid_json; invalid byte encoding produces invalid_utf8. The raw payload is not pre-decoded or repaired by a fixture adapter.
json_and_schema.parse: Strict JSON grammar: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity tokens produce invalid_json. Duplicate decoded object member names use native last-member-wins in both JS and Python. Then validate only the complete resulting object. Do not add a duplicate-reject parser.
json_and_schema.strings: Reject unpaired surrogate code points in every parsed object name/string as invalid_schema. Do not normalize Unicode.
json_and_schema.objects: Each object must be a JSON object, never null/array. Require exactly its stated own members. profiles is a nonempty own-member map of at most 100 valid profiles. Every profile is fully validated, selected or not.
json_and_schema.version: Require a finite integral parsed JSON number, explicitly excluding booleans. Numeric 1, 1.0 and 1e0 are V1. Any other integral value is unsupported_version. Missing/wrong-type/nonfinite/nonintegral is invalid_schema.
json_and_schema.default: Missing default_profile or a valid default name absent from profiles is missing_default_profile. Wrong-type default is invalid_schema; a string failing profile grammar/reserved membership is invalid_profile.
json_and_schema.metadata: key_id, account.id, workspace_id and workspace_name are nonempty strings by length, with no trimming or normalization. account.name is any string including empty, or null. All strings still obey the unpaired-surrogate prohibition. Metadata cannot grant server authority.
json_and_schema.key: api_key must be string and nonempty after fixed trim. Accepted keys use trimmed value. Do not require a prefix.
json_and_schema.base: Every base_url must pass canonicalization and already equal its canonical output; failures are invalid_base_url. Shape/type failures elsewhere are invalid_schema.
json_and_schema.errors: Use the specific earlier read/decode/parse stage error. Structural/schema errors are invalid_schema except the explicit profile, default, version, profile-count and base categories above. Multi-defect combinations assert only priorities expressly specified by a case.

pin_notes: PREPARED_FOR_ROOT_PIN only: coordinator must inspect these exact bytes, record the digest and separately authorize any client source lease.
Canonicalization strips all terminal slashes and is idempotent; strict ASCII file/login URLs reject percent/dot/repair ambiguities. Stored bases are already canonical.
The fixed trim set, full-string profile validation, exact reserved list and native JS-null/Python-None distinction are deliberate public rules.
Decoded duplicate JSON members are last-member-wins, including escaped names; validate the complete resulting document. Duplicate rejection is not part of this contract.
Explicit/environment-key legacy base behavior remains package-specific. File-base explicit invalid/empty overrides shadow environment values and fail locally.
R17-R19 intentionally change required store IO to zero because malformed explicit profile selectors fail before reading the store.
Native reader cases have a 5000 ms bound; writer lock tests record their own configured finite deadline. Native substitutions cannot authorize the replacement identity.
common_identity explicitly requests workspace Research while leaving profile unnamed. Revocation assertions retain typed or projected public semantics and include POST.

steps: One real TS CLI invocation with argv ['login','--workspace','Research'] leaves profile unnamed, requests exactly workspace Research, and saves default into an isolated previously empty home after a local fake exchange. The stored base is the exact explicitly selected test login target.
Use same bytes/home with no key env in packed TS Client, installed Python wheel Client/AsyncClient, TS CLI account or computers read, Python CLI read, and packed MCP stdio read tool.
Backend maps each synthetic key to a distinct account/workspace and records bearer identity internally; serialize only public labels/digests in evidence.
An independently valid default/decoy key must return different identity, so wrong selection cannot pass.
Revoke selected at backend; repeat all clients. Require ordinary typed/error-projected revoked refusal and no fallback; preserve saved file.
